Issued at 254 PM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Weak showers and thunderstorms continue to linger along a
developing warm front in the west. Weak instability and modest
shear along this boundary will linger at least slight chances
through the night in these areas. The threat for severe weather
is overall low given the elevated nature of these storms. The
main threat could be gusty winds given DCAPE is over 1000 J/KG
along this boundary. Otherwise, look for mainly dry conditions
tonight with lows in the mid 50s to mid 60s. Light winds will
become southerly as well for tonight. Warm front moves through
Saturday with a building ridge overhead. This will bring warming
temperatures, yet limited instability. The result will be highs
in the 90s to near 100 degrees. Dry conditions will limit the
heat index values, although there could be some increased Heat
Risk and Wet Bulb Global Temperature Risk. Thus will hold off on
any heat products for Saturday. Developing surface low to the
west will bring an increased southerly flow on Saturday.
Afternoon humidity values in the teens and 20s will be found in
the west, although the breezy winds on Saturday will be more
central and east where afternoon humidity values are forecast in
the 30s and 40s. Thus some increased fire weather concerns are
possible for Saturday, although near critical fire weather
conditions are currently not anticipated. HRRR Smoke also
showing some wildfire smoke may return to the area and perhaps
surface on Saturday. HRRR Smoke even showing some surface smoke
possible across the west Saturday afternoon and evening. With
the southerly flow at the surface there is some uncertainty on
this smoke reaching the surface. Thus held off on adding it to
the forecast at this time. Dry conditions look to continue for
Saturday night, with mild lows in the 60s. Upper level ridge
moves eastward Sunday with the thermal ridge pushing across the
state as well. This will bring slightly warmer temperatures in
the 90s and lower 100s. Increased southerly flow could also
bring slightly higher dewpoints, which will also increase heat
index values. A heat advisory may be needed for Sunday if this
trend continues. A wind advisory may also be needed for these
stronger southerly winds, although ECMWF EFI values may indicate
these winds peak just right around advisory level. These
stronger winds combined with low RH values in the teens and 20s
could bring some near critical to critical fire weather
conditions across western and some central portions Sunday
afternoon and evening. This may depend on timing of a cold front
Sunday afternoon and evening. This front could also bring some
showers and thunderstorms, mainly Sunday night when instability
and shear peaks. A low level jet may also help increase the
threat for thunderstorms Sunday night. Surface capping and
overall timing uncertainties of the mentioned front could be the
limiting factors for the severe weather threat. SPC has
maintained a Marginal Risk for central and eastern portions
Sunday through Sunday night. If thunderstorms can develop,
chances will linger through Sunday night with lows near 60
degrees.

Cold front continues to push through Monday, lingering the
threat for thunderstorms and perhaps some severe weather. SPC
has maintained a Day 4 outlooks for eastern ND on Monday. The
severe weather threat looks similar to Sunday, although also
looks to be in more eastern North Dakota. Otherwise look for
cooler temperatures Monday with breezy north winds. Even with
cooler temperatures, dry conditions behind the front combined
with breezy winds could bring some near critical to critical
fire weather conditions Monday afternoon and evening. A post
frontal cool, breezy, and mainly dry day is then forecast for
Tuesday, with highs in the 70s and morning lows in the upper 40s
to mid 50s. Overall a warming trend is then forecast for mid to
late next week, although a split in clusters showing there could
be a spread in how much warming. It will overall depend if the
ridge can build back into the area or if west to northwest flow
remains. This pattern will also determine chances for
precipitation, although currently a generally dry conditions are
forecast.
